Normal.description: Hemoglobin levels are within the healthy range. Maintain a balanced diet to sustain good health.
Normal.diet_recommendation: Maintain a balanced diet rich in iron sources to prevent future deficiency.
food_list: Nuts and seeds (pumpkin seeds, sunflower seeds)
Citrus fruits for vitamin C to boost iron absorption
foods_to_avoid: Excessive tea or coffee with meals (inhibits iron absorption)
High-phytate foods in excess without vitamin C pairing
Normal.referral_action: No referral required. Schedule routine check-up in 12 months.

Mild.description: Mild reduction in hemoglobin levels. Dietary intervention is the primary recommendation.
Mild.diet_recommendation: Increase consumption of iron-rich foods. Pair with vitamin C sources to enhance absorption. Avoid iron inhibitors at meal times.
food_list: Spinach, Swiss chard, and dark leafy greens
Lean beef and organ meats (liver, kidney)
Vitamin C foods: oranges, bell peppers, strawberries, kiwi
foods_to_avoid: Calcium-rich foods at the same time as iron-rich meals
Mild.supplements: Consider iron supplement (ferrous sulphate) under medical supervision if dietary changes are insufficient.
Mild.referral_action: Recommend follow-up with primary care physician within 4–6 weeks to recheck hemoglobin levels.

Moderate.description: Significant reduction in hemoglobin levels requiring both dietary changes and medical consultation.
Moderate.diet_recommendation: Follow a structured iron-rich diet plan combined with vitamin C at every meal to maximise iron absorption. Medical consultation is recommended.
food_list: Organ meats: liver (beef or chicken) — highest iron content
Red meat (beef, lamb) — 2–3 servings per week
Cooked spinach, lentils, and black beans
Vitamin C at every meal: tomatoes, citrus, bell peppers
foods_to_avoid: Tea, coffee, and cocoa with meals
Antacids and proton pump inhibitors (if possible)
Moderate.supplements: Iron supplementation (ferrous sulphate or ferrous gluconate) required. Vitamin B12 and folate assessment recommended.
Moderate.referral_action: Refer to physician or haematologist within 2 weeks. Blood work panel required including serum ferritin, iron, and TIBC.

Severe.description: Critically low hemoglobin levels. This is a medical emergency requiring immediate professional intervention.
Severe.diet_recommendation: Immediate medical care is the priority. Nutritional support should be initiated alongside medical treatment under clinical supervision.
food_list: High-iron foods as tolerated: liver, red meat, legumes
Iron-fortified liquid nutritional supplements if solid food is not tolerated
Vitamin C with every meal to maximise iron absorption
Folate-rich foods: leafy greens, fortified cereals, asparagus
Vitamin B12 sources: eggs, dairy, meat, or B12-fortified foods
Easily digestible foods to reduce metabolic load
foods_to_avoid: All iron absorption inhibitors: tea, coffee, dairy with meals
Raw vegetables if digestion is compromised
Severe.supplements: IV iron therapy or blood transfusion may be required. Erythropoiesis-stimulating agents under specialist care.
Severe.referral_action: IMMEDIATE MEDICAL REFERRAL required. Emergency evaluation by haematologist or hospital admission may be necessary. Do not delay treatment.
